title: Jackfruit vs. meat: why they are not nutritionally equivalent

seo.title: Jackfruit vs. meat: the protein difference
seo.meta_description: Jackfruit works as a texture substitute, not a protein substitute. Compare protein, fiber and how to build a fuller meal.
seo.search_intent: Understand jackfruit and meat nutrition differences

excerpt: Young jackfruit can mimic shredded-meat texture, but not its protein density: roughly 2–2.6 g/100 g versus about 20 g/100 g in raw 90/10 ground beef.
content_html:
Young jackfruit shreds well and absorbs sauce, but a meat-like texture does not mean meat-like protein.

The protein gap

Young-fruit references are around 2.0–2.6 g protein/100 g. USDA raw 90/10 ground beef provides about 20 g/100 g. At 150 g that is roughly 3–4 g versus about 30 g.

What jackfruit provides

Young fruit contains carbohydrate and roughly 2.6–3.6 g fiber/100 g, with little fat. Meat has no dietary fiber.

Canned jackfruit can be salty

Savory recipes usually use young green jackfruit in brine, and sodium varies widely.

Build protein into the meal

Add beans, lentils, tofu, tempeh or TVP if the goal is also to replace meat's protein.

The useful framing

Treat jackfruit as a plant food with a meat-like texture, not a one-for-one protein replacement.

faq.question: Does jackfruit have as much protein as meat?
faq.answer: No. Young jackfruit is roughly 2–2.6 g/100 g versus about 20 g/100 g in raw 90/10 beef.

faq.question: Does jackfruit contain fiber?
faq.answer: Yes, roughly 2.6–3.6 g/100 g in the cited range.

faq.question: Is canned jackfruit salty?
faq.answer: It can be; check the brine and label.

faq.question: How can I add protein?
faq.answer: Pair it with beans, lentils, tofu, tempeh or TVP.
